Mass ratio \(C:H = 12:1\) gives mole ratio \(\frac{12}{12} : \frac{1}{1} = 1:1\), so the empirical formula is \(CH\). With two carbon atoms the molecular formula is \(C_2H_2\), molar mass \(= 2(12) + 2(1) = 26\ g\ mol^{-1}\).

Moles of hydrocarbon \(= \frac{3.38}{26} = 0.13\ mol\).

Combustion: \(C_2H_2 + \frac{5}{2}O_2 \rightarrow 2CO_2 + H_2O\), so moles of \(CO_2 = 2 \times 0.13 = 0.26\ mol\).

Mass of \(CO_2 = 0.26 \times 44 = 11.44\ g\).

The 0.1 M HCl is a strong acid, so \([H^+] = 0.1\ M\) and this common-ion effect suppresses the ionisation of the very weak acid \(H_2A\) almost completely. Hence \([H_2A] \approx 0.1\ M\).

For the first ionisation \(H_2A \rightleftharpoons H^+ + HA^-\):
\(K_{a1} = \frac{[H^+][HA^-]}{[H_2A]}\)

\([HA^-] = \frac{K_{a1}[H_2A]}{[H^+]} = \frac{(8.1 \times 10^{-8})(0.1)}{0.1} = 8.1 \times 10^{-8}\ M\).

(\(K_{a2}\) is far smaller and removes a negligible amount of \(HA^-\).)

(A) \(BrF_4^-\): \(AX_4E_2\), square planar -- not isostructural.
(B) \(CH_4\): \(AX_4\), tetrahedral -- no.
(C) \(IF_4^+\): valence electrons \(= 7 - 1 = 6\); 4 used in bonding, 1 lone pair left, \(AX_4E\) see-saw -- YES.
(D) \(XeF_4\): \(AX_4E_2\), square planar -- no.
(E) \(XeO_2F_2\): 4 sigma bonds (2 to O, 2 to F) and 1 lone pair on Xe, \(AX_4E\) see-saw -- YES.

Hence (C) and (E) only.

For \(X \rightarrow Y\): \(q = +10\ J\) (absorbed) and work done by the gas \(w_{by} = 18\ J\).
\(\Delta U_{X \rightarrow Y} = q - w_{by} = 10 - 18 = -8\ J\).

Internal energy is a state function, so for \(Y \rightarrow X\), \(\Delta U = +8\ J\). Heat evolved is 6 J, so \(q = -6\ J\).

A negative work done by the gas means 14 J of work is done ON the gas by the surroundings.

Coordination isomerism requires BOTH the cation and the anion to be complex ions, and interchanging the ligand sets between the two metal centres must give a genuinely different compound.

(A) \([Ag(NH_3)_2][Ag(CN)_2]\): both centres are the same metal in the same oxidation state with the same coordination number, so swapping the ligands regenerates the identical compound -- no isomerism.
(B) \([Co(NH_3)_6][Cr(CN)_6]\): swapping gives \([Cr(NH_3)_6][Co(CN)_6]\), a different compound -- YES.
(C) \([Co(NH_3)_6][Co(CN)_6]\): same metal, same oxidation state and coordination number on both sides, so the swap gives the same salt -- no isomerism.
(D) \([Fe(NH_3)_6][Co(CN)_6]\): swapping gives \([Co(NH_3)_6][Fe(CN)_6]\) -- YES.
(E) \([Co(NH_3)_6][Fe(CN)_6]\): swapping gives \([Fe(NH_3)_6][Co(CN)_6]\) -- YES.

Hence B, D and E only.

Start with 4-nitroethylbenzene.

Step 1, \(Br_2/AlBr_3\): the ethyl group is an activating ortho/para director but its para position is blocked by \(-NO_2\); the nitro group is a meta director. Both effects point to the position ortho to ethyl and meta to nitro, so \(A\) is 2-bromo-1-ethyl-4-nitrobenzene.

Step 2, \(Sn/HCl\): reduces \(-NO_2\) to \(-NH_2\), giving \(B\).

Step 3, \(NaNO_2/HCl\) at 273-278 K: diazotisation gives the diazonium salt \(C\).

Step 4, \(C_2H_5OH\): the diazonium group is replaced by hydrogen (reductive deamination), so \(D\) is 1-bromo-2-ethylbenzene.

Step 5, \(KMnO_4/KOH\) then \(H_3O^+\): the ethyl side chain is oxidised completely to \(-COOH\), giving \(E\) = 2-bromobenzoic acid.

Option (B) shows exactly this pair.

The borax bead test gives a coloured bead only with metal ions having partially filled d orbitals. \(Zn^{2+}\) is \(3d^{10}\) and gives a colourless bead, so it is eliminated even though its ionisation enthalpy is large.

Among the remaining coloured ions, \(Fe^{2+}\) (\(3d^6\)), \(Cr^{2+}\) (\(3d^4\)) and \(Fe^{3+}\) (\(3d^5\)), the \(Fe^{3+}\) ion has the exactly half-filled \(3d^5\) configuration, which is extra stable; removing a further electron from it requires the largest energy, so it has the highest ionisation enthalpy of the three.

Hence \(Fe^{3+}\).

Let the initial pressure of \(A\) be \(P_0\) and let \(x\) be the pressure of \(C\) formed at time \(t\). From \(2A \rightarrow 4B + C\), \(A\) falls by \(2x\) and \(B\) rises by \(4x\):

\(P_{total} = (P_0 - 2x) + 4x + x = P_0 + 3x\).

At \(t = \infty\) all of \(A\) is consumed, so \(2x = P_0\), i.e. \(x = \frac{P_0}{2}\) and
\(P_{\infty} = P_0 + \frac{3P_0}{2} = \frac{5P_0}{2} = 600 \Rightarrow P_0 = 240\) mm Hg.

At \(t = 30\) min: \(240 + 3x = 300 \Rightarrow x = 20\).

Since \(x\) is itself the partial pressure of \(C\), \(P_C = 20\) mm Hg.

\(E^{\circ}_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{cathode} - E^{\circ}_{anode} = 1.23 - 0.02 = 1.21\ V\), with \(n = 6\) electrons per mole of \(CH_3OH\).

Maximum work \(= -\Delta G^{\circ} = nFE^{\circ}_{cell} = 6 \times 96500 \times 1.21 = 700590\ J\).
